Branches have no update route, so changing any argument replaces the branch and discards its data. A branch given a `ttl` is deleted by the server when it expires; the next refresh then drops it from state and the following plan recreates it.

api.description: The product API that owns this database.

connection_password.description: The password to connect with. Rotate it out of band; this provider only reads it.

connection_string.description: The full connection URI, including credentials.

container_status.description: The container status for lifecycle-managed runtimes.

created_at.description: The database creation timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

engine.description: The database engine reported by the server.

error.description: The error message reported by the server when the status is `failed`.

id.description: The database ID. Must be unique within the project. Generated when omitted. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

idle_timeout_minutes.description: Minutes of inactivity, from 5 to 60, before the database container scales to zero. Applies to shared-pool specifications only.

idle_until.description: When the database is expected to be considered idle, in ISO 8601 format.

last_accessed_at.description: The last activity timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

maintenance_window_day.description: The day of the week the maintenance window starts. One of `sun`, `mon`, `tue`, `wed`, `thu`, `fri` or `sat`. Must be set together with `maintenance_window_hour_utc`.

maintenance_window_hour_utc.description: The hour in UTC (0-23) the maintenance window starts. Must be set together with `maintenance_window_day`.

network_idle_timeout_seconds.description: How long an idle client connection is held open before the server closes it.

network_ip_allowlist.description: IP addresses and CIDR ranges allowed to connect. An empty set allows any address.

network_max_connections.description: The maximum number of concurrent client connections.

node_pool.description: The node pool the database is scheduled on.

pitr_retention_days.description: How many days of point-in-time recovery data to retain.

project_id.description: The Appwrite project ID. Defaults to the provider-level project_id. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

replicas.description: The number of high availability replicas. High availability is enabled when greater than 0.

specification.description: The compute specification slug, for example `s-1vcpu-1gb`. Read the available slugs from the corresponding specifications data source. Changing this resizes the database in place.

sql_api_max_rows.description: The maximum number of rows returned per SQL API execution. Larger results are truncated.

sql_api_timeout_seconds.description: The maximum server-side SQL API execution time in seconds before a query is canceled.

ssl.description: Whether SSL/TLS is required for client connections.

status.description: The desired database status. Set to `paused` to stop the database without deleting it, and back to `ready` to resume it. Left unset, the status is only read back from the server.

storage_autoscaling.description: Whether storage expands automatically as it fills up.

storage_autoscaling_max_gb.description: The storage ceiling in GB for autoscaling. 0 means no limit.

storage_autoscaling_threshold_percent.description: The storage usage percentage that triggers automatic expansion.

storage_class.description: The storage class backing the volume.

storage_max_gb.description: The maximum storage allowed in GB. 0 means the system default.

sync_mode.description: The replication sync mode. One of `async`, `sync` or `quorum`. Only meaningful when `replicas` is greater than 0.

updated_at.description: The database last update timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

version.description: The MongoDB engine version. Changing this performs an in-place major version upgrade, which cannot be rolled back.

block.description: Enables or disables the ways users can sign in to a project. Requests made with an API key are not affected. Every project has these settings, so creating this resource takes them over rather than creating anything, and destroying it resets them to Appwrite's defaults. An attribute left out of the configuration is set to its default too. Use one per project: two would overwrite each other.

deny_aliased_email.description: Whether signing up or changing email address is refused for an aliased address, such as one with a `+` suffix. Defaults to `false`.

deny_corporate_email.description: Whether signing up or changing email address is restricted to corporate addresses, refusing addresses at free or disposable email domains. Despite the name, which follows Appwrite's policy ID, it is non-corporate addresses that are denied. Defaults to `false`.

deny_disposable_email.description: Whether signing up or changing email address is refused for an address at a known disposable email domain. Defaults to `false`.

deny_free_email.description: Whether signing up or changing email address is refused for an address at a free email provider such as Gmail or Yahoo. Defaults to `false`.

id.description: The project ID.

user_accessed_at.description: Whether members can see when other members last accessed the project. Defaults to `false`.

user_email.description: Whether members can see each other's email address. Defaults to `false`.

user_id.description: Whether members can see each other's user ID. Defaults to `false`.

user_mfa.description: Whether members can see if other members have MFA enabled. Defaults to `false`.

user_name.description: Whether members can see each other's name. Defaults to `false`.

user_phone.description: Whether members can see each other's phone number. Defaults to `false`.

membership_privacy.description: Which details of a team member the other members of the team can see. Leaving it out sets every field to its default.

custom.description: Whether a code delivered through your own channel can be used. Defaults to `false`.

email.description: Whether a code sent by email can be used. Defaults to `true`.

phone.description: Whether a code sent by SMS can be used. Defaults to `true`.

totp.description: Whether an authenticator app (TOTP) can be used. Defaults to `true`.

mfa_factors.description: Which factors users can complete an MFA challenge with. Recovery codes always remain available. Leaving it out sets every field to its default.

password_dictionary.description: Whether a new password is rejected when it is one of the 10,000 most common passwords. Existing passwords stay valid. Defaults to `false`.

password_history.description: How many of a user's previous passwords they cannot reuse, from 1 to 20, or `0` to keep no history. Passwords are only recorded while the history is kept, so turning it on does not cover passwords set before. Defaults to `0`.

password_personal_data.description: Whether a new password is rejected when it contains the user's ID, name, email address or phone number. Existing passwords stay valid. Defaults to `false`.

enabled.description: Whether passwords are checked when a user signs up, signs in or sets a password. On its own this only records the result on the user. Defaults to `true`.

sessions.description: Whether signing in with a breached password is refused until the password is reset. Defaults to `false`.

users.description: Whether a breached password is rejected when a user signs up or sets a new password. Defaults to `false`.

password_pwned.description: Checks passwords against the Have I Been Pwned breach database. Only the first five characters of the password's hash are sent to it. Requires Appwrite 2.3.0 or later; against an older server, any value other than the defaults fails to apply. Leaving it out sets every field to its default.

lowercase.description: Whether it must contain a lowercase letter. Defaults to `false`.

min.description: The minimum length, from 8 to 256. Defaults to `8`.

number.description: Whether it must contain a digit. Defaults to `false`.

symbols.description: Whether it must contain a symbol. Defaults to `false`.

uppercase.description: Whether it must contain an uppercase letter. Defaults to `false`.

password_strength.description: What a new password must contain. Leaving it out sets every field to its default.

project_id.description: The Appwrite project ID. Defaults to the provider-level project_id. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

session_alert.description: Whether a user is emailed when a new session is created for them. The first session after signing up does not send one. Defaults to `false`.

index.description: The member index. Read `role` for which member accepts writes: a failover moves the primary without renumbering.

lag_seconds.description: Replication lag in seconds. 0 for the primary, and for a streaming member whose engine printed no numeric lag.

replicating.description: Whether the member is streaming from the primary. False for a primary, which has no stream to report, and for an unhealthy member, which is not probed.

role.description: `primary`, `replica`, or `unknown` while a transition is moving the topology.

replicas.description: Every configured member, including one the backend has not brought up, which is reported as not healthy.

sync_acknowledgements.description: How many standby acknowledgements the primary waits for before committing a write.

sync_degraded.description: Whether the enforced replication is weaker than the requested `sync_mode`.

sync_standby_count.description: How many standbys are registered with the primary for synchronous replication.

sync_state_confirmed.description: Whether the sync fields are an engine reading rather than a recorded estimate. False means no reading was taken, not that replication is unhealthy — draw no conclusion about replication health from it.

volumes.description: The storage volumes backing the database.

block.description:
Reads the live operational state of a dedicated Appwrite PostgreSQL database: health, replication, connection counts and storage volumes.
